subject.title: Factory Track A: generalize observed coding-agent sessions into a SessionObserver seam with a durable registry

question: Should this remain a broad generic Factory track, or be narrowed to the event and adoption gaps left after current Codex supervision landed?
rationale: Current main already solves much of Codex discovery and binding, while canonical cross-runtime identity, shared persistence, adoption semantics, and public observer APIs are durable product choices that automation cannot select safely.

options.title: Narrow remaining gaps
options.body: Keep observed records Codex-owned, add push-driven session-state events and adoption metadata, and defer generic API extraction until another observer demonstrates the shared need.

options.title: Sponsor broad core model
options.body: Approve canonical observed-session identity, a shared registry, a public observer API, lineage, and adoption UX as a coordinated architecture program.

options.title: Defer further work
options.body: Treat the current Codex catalog and binding capability as sufficient until another coding runtime or concrete user workflow demonstrates demand.

recommendation.title: Narrow remaining gaps
recommendation.body: Keep observed records Codex-owned, add push-driven session-state events and adoption metadata, and defer generic API extraction until another observer demonstrates the shared need.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across current Codex supervision, the session-state substrate, and this proposed Factory direction.
